title: Meta reorganises its AI work as Meta Superintelligence Labs
summary: In an internal memo, Mark Zuckerberg said "developing superintelligence is coming into sight" and grouped Meta's AI teams under a new unit led by Alexandr Wang. He described the goal as "personal superintelligence for everyone".

title: Open letter calls for a prohibition on superintelligence
summary: The Future of Life Institute released the Statement on Superintelligence, calling for a ban on its development until there is broad scientific consensus it can be done safely and strong public support. More than 700 people signed at launch, including Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio.

title: Microsoft forms the MAI Superintelligence Team
summary: Mustafa Suleyman, head of Microsoft AI, announced a team working towards "humanist superintelligence". He described it as advanced AI kept within limits and in service of people, rather than an unbounded system.

title: Sanders and Casar introduce the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act
summary: The bill would ban building AI that could "destroy or disempower humanity", pause advanced AI development until a regulator sets safety rules, and create a cabinet-level Department of Artificial Intelligence. Violations could bring up to 20 years in prison.

title: Executive order "Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence" signed
summary: US federal agencies are told to replace "artificial intelligence" and "AI" with "super intelligence" and "SI" in official communications. Statutes and contracts are not rewritten.

title: Six AI companies sign the voluntary White House Accord on Super Intelligence
summary: Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI and xAI commit to internal oversight, independent audits and board review. The accord carries no legal penalties.

title: Elon Musk says SpaceXAI will be renamed SpaceXSI
summary: Replying on X after the US executive order, Musk confirmed the AI arm of SpaceX would switch to the new term: "No more AI. SI, it's better."

title: The White House Super Intelligence Force holds its first meeting and adopts its charter
summary: The task force chaired by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton began a 120-day review of how AI labs report breaches, hacks and jailbreaks to the government. Its leaders warned companies that delayed notification "will not be tolerated", according to The Next Web.

title: The State Department orders staff to write "SI" instead of "AI"
summary: A department-wide cable reported by Nextgov/FCW tells personnel to use "super intelligence" in new letters, websites, reports and the names of programs and governance bodies. Legal citations, contracts and grants are excluded, and published titles such as America's AI Action Plan are kept.

title: The US Navy and Marine Corps switch to "super intelligence" in official documents
summary: A Navy administrative message (NAVADMIN 252/26) requires "SI" in place of "AI" across correspondence, training materials and fleet advisories, and the Marine Corps issued a similar memo the next day. Stars and Stripes reported that the Army and Air Force are also making the change.

title: Representative Yassamin Ansari calls for a ban on artificial superintelligence
summary: The day after the midterm elections, the Arizona Democrat posted on X that Democrats in Congress should make AI regulation an early priority, including a "pause on advanced AI development" and a "ban on artificial superintelligence", as reported by Tom's Hardware.

title: The Justice Department launches a Super Intelligence Task Force
summary: The task force, led by Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward and Associate Deputy Attorney General Stephen Weiss, targets misuse of SI by foreign state actors, criminal organisations and fraudsters. Attorney General Todd Blanche said it will work with the Super Intelligence Force chaired by Jay Clayton.

title: Trump says he is "100% in favor of Super Intelligence"
summary: In a Truth Social post, the president called the technology "GOLD" and said he would work with US states that want to profit from it, according to Anadolu Agency.

title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent previews a US-China dialogue on superintelligence
summary: Speaking to the National Committee on US-China Relations in New York, Bessent said the two countries would share methods for testing advanced models and keeping humans in control, and use a direct channel to report serious incidents. He said the dialogue should advance at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, according to TokenPost.

title: EU governments push back on "super intelligence" wording in a US-led alliance declaration
summary: EU ambassadors discussed a US draft declaration for the Pax Silica alliance that promotes the superintelligence concept. The European Commission proposed a note stating the EU reads the term as meaning artificial intelligence, as defined in the AI Act, Euronews reported.
